original_question: For the class of pro-countable groups viewed as closed subgroups of S∞, is the isomorphism relation not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism, or even analytic complete?
target_in_paper: Problem 22 in Section 6 (Andre Nies), subsection "Complexity of isomorphism of oligomorphic groups": "Is there a Borel, invariant class of closed subgroups of S∞ with isomorphism relation not Borel below graph isomorphism? Analytic complete? How about the class of pro-countable groups?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the paper's intended candidate class—pro-countable groups among closed subgroups of S∞—and it preserves the two exact complexity directions asked in the paper: whether the relevant isomorphism relation is not Borel reducible to countable graph isomorphism, and whether it might even be analytic-complete.
missing_details: The official formulation first asks for the existence of some Borel, isomorphism-invariant class of closed subgroups of S∞ with the stated complexity, and only then asks whether the class of pro-countable groups could be such a class.
The ambient coding space should be made explicit: the standard Borel space of closed subgroups of S∞.
The class in question should be stated to be Borel in that coding space, not just a class considered abstractly.
The invariance requirement is implicit in the paper but missing from the draft: the class should be invariant under the relevant isomorphism relation.
In the surrounding subsection, the relevant equivalence relation is topological isomorphism of closed subgroups of S∞, not merely abstract group isomorphism.
The inherited Polish topology from S∞ is part of the setup and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation.
“Graph isomorphism” should be spelled out as isomorphism of countable graphs.
“Analytic complete” should be spelled out as analytic-complete among analytic equivalence relations under Borel reducibility.
If the question is stated specifically for pro-countable groups, it should be framed as asking whether that class furnishes an example answering the broader existence question posed in Problem 22.
refined_question: Let Subg(S∞) denote the standard Borel space of closed subgroups of the full symmetric group S∞ on N, each equipped with its inherited Polish topology, and let ≅top denote topological group isomorphism. Does there exist a Borel ≅top-invariant class C ⊆ Subg(S∞) such that ≅top restricted to C is not Borel reducible to isomorphism of countable graphs, or even is analytic-complete among analytic equivalence relations under Borel reducibility? In particular, can one take C to be the class of pro-countable groups?
justification: The draft is aiming at the last sentence of Problem 22, which is the nearest official formulation in the paper. The paper does not state the pro-countable case as a separate standalone conjecture; rather, it asks first for a Borel invariant class of closed subgroups of S∞ whose isomorphism relation lies above the graph-isomorphism benchmark, possibly up to analytic completeness, and then proposes pro-countable groups as the candidate class. The nearby context also matters: Problem 19 explicitly discusses topological isomorphism for oligomorphic groups, and Theorem 20 sits in the same subsection and provides the surrounding structural/topological context. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should keep the Borel/invariant-class setup and make explicit that the intended relation is topological isomorphism on closed subgroups of S∞.
